chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Sayyari from Abu Yazid al-Qasmi (and Qasim is a tribe from Yemen in Basra) from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him): that he asked him.
About the skins of the Darish (a type of goat/sheep) from which slippers are made, so he said: 'Do not pray in them, for they are tanned with the dung of dogs.'

key_terms.الدَّارِش: A type of goat or sheep, specifically referenced here for its skin used in footwear.
key_terms.تُدْبَغُ: They are tanned (processed to make leather).

ai.seo_question: Are slippers made from Darish skins suitable for prayer if tanned with dog dung?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) ruled that one should not pray in footwear made from the skins of Darish animals because they are tanned using dog dung, which renders them impure or unsuitable for prayer. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the tanning process determines the purity of animal skins, with dog dung serving as a specific agent of impurity (najasa) that invalidates the garment for ritual prayer.
